context: Session 12, run mrun-20d9230f767b, feature 078-verification-receipts. Four open blocks that require engineer input. Q-01 is the session's designated first action and blocks it outright. Q-02 gates two of Q-01's six items, so answering Q-02 first may partly answer Q-01. Q-03 is a half-blocked prior ruling (Q-GLPNETS11-02) that cannot be executed as written. Q-04 is past its own 8-hour escalation window by three days. Every verdict cited here was measured this session, not carried from the prior restart document.

questions.question: The 078 discharge gate refuses on 6 checklist items. I measured each: 2 are satisfied (codexreview run 20260828T004446Z is on disk, exit 0, 752s, and 078's finding arc converged 10 to 4 to 1 to 1; release v2026.08.28.1 is tagged on merge c9d32d90 with main and develop reconciled). 3 genuinely fail: implement is 4 of 66 tasks; there is no 078 retrospective among the 21 in .specify/retrospective; and SC-001 demands 13 named witnessed instances fault-injected, but the harness has 11 modules naming only instances 2 and 9 -- coverage is an anonymous tally, so faultinj 51/51 green does not demonstrate 13 of 13. 1 is satisfied at repo level only: a ship happened, but it shipped the repo while 078 stood at 4 of 66. How much of this gate do you want waived?

options.label: Waive 2+3, run close, hold 1+5+6
options.means: Record the two satisfied items as discharged by citation; run /bk-close 078 to produce the genuinely-missing retrospective; leave implement, SC-001 coverage and the adoption narrowing standing until Q-02 rules and a case-keyed instance registry exists.
options.cost: 078 stays open across at least one more session, and the era remains uncloseable meanwhile. The run's outstanding count does not drop.

options.label: Waive all six, close the era
options.means: Record a full informed-consent override on the ground that the code shipped in v2026.08.28.1 and the feature has converged; close 078 now and reclaim the single active pipeline slot for 082 or the next feature.
options.cost: Waives SC-001, which is 078's OWN acceptance criterion. By 078's own FR-016 an unexercised declared case must read UNREAD, never green -- so this closes the feature on exactly the failure mode the feature exists to prevent, and every future green run in this repo inherits that ambiguity.

options.label: Waive nothing, build item 5 first
options.means: Leave the gate fully intact. Next session's first code task is the case-keyed 13-instance registry, mirroring what faultinj/conformance.py already does right with _CASES self-registration. Re-attempt discharge only once SC-001 is genuinely demonstrable.
options.cost: The two genuinely-satisfied items keep generating a refusal that is now known to be spurious, which trains the lane to read the gate's output as noise -- the same reflex-to-override defect flagged against the secret scanner.

decision.label: Waive 2+3, run close, hold 1+5+6
decision.rationale: Recorded ruling; written back from engineer-decisions.jsonl (answer='Waive 2+3, close, hold 1+5+6', an abbreviation of this label — sole match).

questions.question: 55 of 078's 66 tasks carry a bk: prefix, meaning they belong to the buildkit repository, not glpnet. glpnet holds the spec, the contracts and a working reference implementation under codeconv/src/codeconv/receipts; buildkit is where the shipped receipts package is supposed to live and where 3rtask and codexreview run. Consequently manifest.py narrows FR-017's six declared areas to the five that are glpnet's, declaring 3rtask and codexreview buildkit-side. Two of Q-01's six checklist items reduce entirely to this. Where does 078 actually get finished?

options.label: Split 11 / 55
options.means: Formally re-scope 078 in glpnet to the 11 glpnet-side tasks and the five glpnet areas, record the 55 bk: tasks as a buildkit-owned successor feature with 078 as its spec of record, and let manifest.py's five-area narrowing stand as correct rather than as an undischarged deviation.
options.cost: FR-017's six-area guarantee is then satisfied by no single repo, so a fleet-wide adoption claim needs both repos read together -- exactly the cross-repo reporting gap 078 was written to close.

options.label: glpnet implements all 66 locally
options.means: Treat the bk: prefix as advisory and build the whole receipts package inside glpnet, shipping it from here.
options.cost: Creates a second implementation of a contract whose FR-024 explicitly prohibits copying between repositories -- the divergence 078 names as one of its own witnessed failures.

options.label: Hand 078 wholly to buildkit
options.means: Close 078 in glpnet as spec-only, transfer the entire feature to the buildkit lane, and consume the result here once shipped.
options.cost: Discards the working codeconv reference implementation and the four rounds of adversarial review already invested in it, and puts this lane's most-advanced feature on another lane's schedule.

decision.label: Split 11 / 55
decision.rationale: Recorded ruling; written back from engineer-decisions.jsonl (answer='Split 11 / 55').

questions.question: Ruling Q-GLPNETS11-02 said to link the 6 unbound pipeline feature ids. It cannot be executed as written: link and link --auto both return 'no new spec directories matched a promoted feature'. All six spec directories exist but no roadmap feature matches by slug or by basename -- 031-gleam-port-spike, 036-glp-gleam-baseline-program, 039-m2-0-verify-erlang-monitor-atomvm, 049-wave1-guard-link-acceptance, 050-full-gleam-combined, 060-wave3-full-gleam-chain. Five are gleam-related and the only gleam roadmap feature already holds one spec_path; 050 is under archive ruling Q-GLPNETS1-04 and must not be linked at all. Separately, 73 of 122 features carry no spec_path and can never bind by basename. reconcile therefore reports NOT-in-sync every round. What should happen to the six?

options.label: Create five, archive 050
options.means: Author five new roadmap features matching the five live gleam spec directories so link can bind them, and record 050 as permanently inert under its existing archive ruling.
options.cost: Adds five features to a roadmap already carrying 28 not-closed rows, and the five are gleam work nobody is scheduled to do -- so the count grows without the work advancing.

options.label: Accept all six inert
options.means: Record a standing acceptance that these six pipeline records bind nothing by design, and treat reconcile's not-in-sync as expected rather than actionable.
options.cost: reconcile's honest warning becomes background noise, which is the precise failure class 078 exists to close -- a mechanism reporting a real divergence that everyone has learned to ignore.

options.label: Leave as-is, re-raise in two weeks
options.means: Change nothing; keep the warning loud and revisit once the gleam workstream has an owner.
options.cost: Every reconcile round for the next fortnight ends NOT-in-sync, and each session spends effort re-establishing that this is known.

decision.label: Create five, archive 050
decision.rationale: Recorded ruling; written back from engineer-decisions.jsonl (answer='Create five, archive 050').

questions.question: Ruling Q-GLPNETS11-01 was 'hold; peers rebase' for two peer branches: 095-shiras (21 commits) and 096-host-interconnectivity (4 commits). They were held deliberately because 096 carries rollForward latestFeature against Q-GLPNETS10-01, which set latestPatch fleet-wide, and both add the Directory.Build.props that Q-GLPNETS10-03 deprecates in favour of the root .targets. The ruling set an 8-hour escalation window. That window expired roughly three days ago and 25 commits of peer work remain stranded. Do you accept continuing to hold?

options.label: Escalate, keep holding
options.means: Send an addressed COOP escalation to shiras and the 096 owner naming both conflicts, hold the merge until they rebase, and re-raise automatically in 7 days.
options.cost: The peers' 25 commits stay unmerged for at least another round-trip on an asynchronous channel where a prior ask went 131 minutes without an ACK and four lanes were silent in one hour.

options.label: Merge, fix conflicts here
options.means: Take both branches, convert rollForward to latestPatch and migrate Directory.Build.props to the root .targets in the merge commit, then notify the owners of what was changed.
options.cost: Edits two peers' work without their agreement on a ruling they may not have seen, and this lane would then own a build-configuration change it did not author and cannot test on their hosts.

options.label: Release the hold, merge as-is
options.means: Merge both branches unmodified and let the fleet rulings be reconciled later.
options.cost: Knowingly lands two violations of standing fleet rulings Q-GLPNETS10-01 and Q-GLPNETS10-03, after which every host inherits a rollForward setting the fleet has already ruled against.

decision.label: Escalate, keep holding
decision.rationale: Recorded ruling; written back from engineer-decisions.jsonl (answer='Escalate, keep holding').
